Sprint 2 rules, taken from https://csci-435-se.github.io/sprint2/, the schedule and the syllabus on 2026-10-14. Re-fetch before relying on this. Anything the Sprint 2 page doesn't state falls back to [[sprint1-requirements]].

**Dates and stakes:** Oct 13 – Oct 29, 2026. Everything is due **Oct 29, 11:59 PM**, except D7, due **Oct 22, 11:59 PM**. The page says 100 points and 10% of the grade; the syllabus says 12%. Lightning talk on Oct 20 covers Sprints 1–2 (requirements at /presentations/, not yet read).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no report (D8) or no release (D9) means 0 for the whole sprint.
- **Late policy (syllabus):** 2-hour grace, then 10% off per day.
- **Load:** same as Sprint 1. CSCI 435 owns at least 2 medium issues; CSCI 535 adds one small. Either can be met with equivalent story points instead.

| D | Pts | Who | Requirement and location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | 10 | Team | `Sprint 2` milestone with every selected issue; estimates; carryover decisions documented on each Sprint 1 issue not taken. |
| D2 | 20 | Indiv | Owner writes or refines the spec before coding; user story, INVEST, ACs; teammate review comment. |
| D3 | 5 | Indiv | At least 1 non-trivial decision per issue, with **at least 2 named alternatives** (now strictly enforced). Otherwise "same format as Sprint 1": due "before or during implementation" (Sprint 1 page), so an empty Design section is fine at spec review; it must be filled before the PR (COURSE-WORKFLOW.md). Issue body, issue comment or PR description all count. |
| D4 | 20 | Indiv | Merged PRs, per-PR rubric unchanged (ACs 6, tests 5, description 4, CI 3, rubric review 2). **New: every PR body needs `## Tech Debt` with `**Introduced:**` and `**Encountered:**`** ("None." is valid). |
| D5 | 5 | Indiv | Logs in `ai-logs/sprint2/<user>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<slug>.md`. Link from an issue **or PR** comment, and link **the file itself**, not a folder or another issue. Full prompts and output; no summaries or screenshots. |
| D6 | 15 | Indiv | **New.** UML for one medium issue you resolved, or several small issues that add up to one medium: in `docs/sprint2/diagrams/`, `<issue#>-<user>-class.png`, `<issue#>-<user>-sequence.png` (or .pdf), and `<issue#>-<user>.md` embedding both plus Q&A (3 class, 3 sequence, 1 AI-use). Mark existing vs new code; annotate; add a note mapping Go structs/interfaces/embedding to UML. |
| D7 | 5 | Indiv | **New.** `docs/sprint2/checkin/<user>.md`, about 150 words each on: what's done and what remains; one thing learned; one thing you'd do differently. Late or thin scores 3. |
| D8 | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint2/report.md`: milestone link, why the team chose these issues, Sprint 1 carryovers, D6/D7 in the deliverables summary, AI-log summary, release link. |
| D9 | 2 | Team | Tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` plus a GitHub release. The page's example says `v2.17.2`; this fork's base is v1.27.3 (s0 and s1 tags). |

#56 is ab-wm's central keyboard-shortcut registry. The user's #57 (`?` dialog), #60 (turn shortcuts off) and #95 (`r` quote reply) all build on it. #65 does not, so it can start first. See [[sprint2-deliverables]].

**Merged 2026-10-19** via PR #96 (as of 10-22 ab-wm's open PR #97 for #58 adds `initShortcutLink`, an additive change), so #57, #58, #59 and #95 are unblocked; #60 is still blocked by #57. Branch from `main` now.

**State on 2026-10-18 (history):** the code was on branch `origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, with the last commit on 10-18. It had no PR and was not merged. ab-wm's spec reviews on all four issues said to "pay attention to the changes introduced by #56".

**API on that branch** (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`):
- `registerShortcut({keys, description, section?, element?, action})` registers a shortcut. `keys` is a space-separated sequence, such as `"g c"`. `description` and `section` arrive already translated from the server, through data attributes or a placeholder. A shortcut with an `element` lives only while that element is connected. Exact or prefix clashes throw.
- `getShortcuts()` returns the list that #57's dialog reads.
- `handleKeyDown` is the only dispatch point, where #60's off switch goes. It skips inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable, modifier keys, and events another handler already prevented.
- `initShortcutKbd` registers `s` and `t` from `<kbd>` hints, under the section "Repository". Nothing registers `?` yet.
- Unit tests are in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`.

**Why:** ab-wm owns #56, and the API can change before it merges. The specs for #57, #60 and #95 name these functions, so a rename means updating those issue bodies too.

**How to apply:** before implementing #57, #60 or #95, check the state live. Use `gh pr list --search 56` and `git log origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, and re-read `shortcut.ts`. Branch from `main` only after #56 merges; never merge ab-wm's branch into the user's own branch (COURSE-WORKFLOW). If #56 is late, raise it with ab-wm early, because a sprint with no merged PR scores 0.

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56
- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, and focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens. It has one row for each shortcut that #56's `getShortcuts()` returns on that page, with the shortcut's keys and description.

- The setting that turns shortcuts off. #60 adds that setting to this dialog as a checkbox.
**Consequences:** The browser provides most of AC2 and AC3, and the dialog needs no jQuery. Browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens to key presses on the whole document, so the dialog must stop other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). This is the first native `<dialog>` in Gitea. No shared helper exists, and the dialog needs its own CSS to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css`.
**Rationale:** The #56 registry already receives its descriptions and section labels as text that the server translated into the page. A dialog that the server renders follows the same pattern. Option (a) is possible, because `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`. But (a) splits the dialog's text between two mechanisms, and it builds markup in JavaScript that the template can hold. Option (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list. `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against Vue for markup this simple.

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a keyboard user who suspects Gitea has shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on any page and see the shortcuts that work on that page, grouped by section, so that I can learn them without reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is on a repository's home page and presses `?`. A dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens in the middle of the page. It lists `?` under "General". It lists `S` ("Search code…") and `T` ("Go to file") under "Repository". Each row shows the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to the description. Focus moves into the dialog, and Tab never reaches the page behind it. The user presses Escape. The dialog closes, and focus returns to where it was.

On the notifications page, no shortcuts belong to the page itself. There, `?` opens the same dialog and lists only `?`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, and focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens. It has one row for each shortcut that #56's `getShortcuts()` returns on that page, with the shortcut's keys and description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then the dialog closes and focus returns to the element that had focus before the dialog opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus never reaches a control on the page behind the dialog.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, a textarea or an editable area, when the user types `?`, then a `?` character appears in the field and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut that later code registers with a new section appears under that section, with no change to the dialog's code.
- [ ] AC6: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the title, the close button's accessible name and the "General" heading come from locale keys.
- [ ] AC7: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses `?` again, then the dialog stays open and unchanged, and no error occurs.
- [ ] AC8: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses the key of another shortcut on the page, then that shortcut does not run. For example, `s` on a repository home page does not move focus to the code search box.
- [ ] AC9: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC8 on a repository home page and calls `assertNoJsError`. Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover the grouping in AC5.

## Out of Scope
- Shortcuts other than `?`. The `g` shortcuts are #58, `c` is #59, and `r` is #95. Each one appears in the dialog when its issue registers it.
- Shortcuts that belong to other pages. The dialog lists only what works on the current page.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The setting that turns shortcuts off. #60 adds that setting to this dialog as a checkbox.
- A link to the dialog in the footer or in a menu.
- A printable list or a documentation page of shortcuts.

## Open Questions
- Should the user also be able to open the dialog with the mouse, for example from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue. One way in keeps the e2e test complete.
- Should a click on the backdrop close the dialog? Proposed: no. Escape and the close button are then the only ways out. Reviewer to confirm.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element and open it with `showModal()`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A Fomantic modal that `showFomanticModal` in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts` opens. Gitea's other modals use this today.
- (b) A plain `<div>` with a focus trap, a backdrop and an Escape handler written by hand.

**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and that new features must not use it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal in an accessibility feature works against #25. `showModal()` makes the page behind the dialog inert (AC3), closes the dialog on Escape (AC2) and sets `aria-modal`. Option (b) would rewrite behaviour that the browser already has, and hand-written focus handling causes the kind of bug that #25 fixes.

**Consequences:** The browser provides most of AC2 and AC3, and the dialog needs no jQuery. Browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens to key presses on the whole document, so the dialog must stop other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). This is the first native `<dialog>` in Gitea. No shared helper exists, and the dialog needs its own CSS to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css`.

### Decision 2: render the dialog's markup and text on the server
**Decision:** Render the empty `<dialog>` once in the base page template, next to the footer script, and keep it hidden until it opens. The server renders the translated title, close label and "General" heading. When the user presses `?`, JavaScript adds the rows from `getShortcuts()`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Build the whole dialog in JavaScript, and add its strings to `window.config.i18n` in `templates/base/head_script.tmpl`.
- (b) A Vue component that mounts on demand and receives its strings as `data-locale-*` attributes.

**Rationale:** The #56 registry already receives its descriptions and section labels as text that the server translated into the page. A dialog that the server renders follows the same pattern. Option (a) is possible, because `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`. But (a) splits the dialog's text between two mechanisms, and it builds markup in JavaScript that the template can hold. Option (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list. `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against Vue for markup this simple.

**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. The `s` and `t` shortcuts register from a `<kbd>` hint on the page, but `?` has no hint. JavaScript registers `?` instead, and reads its description and "General" label from data attributes on the dialog.

## Scope
medium (5 points)

import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
  registerShortcut({
    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: link,
    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

import {ShortcutRegistry, getShortcuts, initGlobalShortcut, initShortcutKbd, initShortcutLink} from './shortcut.ts';

function setup() {
  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <button type="button">button</button>
    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
  `;
  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
  document.body.append(root);
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
    const action = vi.fn();
    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
    return action;
  };
  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

// these tests share document.body and fake timers, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('ShortcutRegistry', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  let ctx: ReturnType<typeof setup>;
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    ctx = setup();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    ctx.cleanup();
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  test('AC3 a single key runs its action once and nothing else', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('?');
    expect(press(ctx.button, '?', {shiftKey: true}).defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(action).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'x').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC3 keys match regardless of case', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('S');
    press(ctx.button, 'S', {shiftKey: true});
    press(ctx.button, 's');
    expect(action).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  test('AC4 pressing Shift in the middle of a sequence does not drop it', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    press(ctx.button, 'Shift', {shiftKey: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'C', {shiftKey: true});
    expect(sequence).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu`, `aria-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |
| `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` | `registerShortcut` (keys like `'g c'`), `getShortcuts`, and the `<kbd data-shortcut-keys data-shortcut-section>` hints and `onShortcutLink` links that register themselves |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already on many pages, not new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** `?_ui_performance_trace=1` prints per-init timings; over 500ms is logged.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Add a keyboard shortcut.** Call `registerShortcut` (`modules/shortcut.ts`). One given an `element`
exists while that element is in the document, hidden or not; a clash with a live one throws. A link
can declare one that follows it (`onShortcutLink`, `templates/repo/header.tmpl`), live while it's
rendered; markup rendered twice (navbar icons, `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl`) marks one copy.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A page-load init without its early return costs every page in Gitea; the 500ms warning catches it.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related

- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions

# i18n — locale files and translation

**Read when:** adding or changing any user-visible string.
**Not here:** using a key in a template -> `templates.md`; in TypeScript -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

The translated strings and the machinery that looks them up, for both the backend/templates and
the frontend.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | **the only file you edit** — the source of truth |
| `options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` | 28 other locales, all generated from Crowdin |
| `modules/translation/translation.go` | locale loading and lookup; requires the `locale_*.json` naming |
| `modules/translation/i18n/` | the lookup implementation and fallback behaviour |
| `crowdin.yml` | the sync config: source is `locale_en-US.json`, translations land as `locale_%locale%.json` |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- A `data-` attribute carrying a translated string to TypeScript is read with `getAttribute` and
  usually named for its use (`data-tooltip-content`, read in `web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`). Vue
  mounts often use `data-locale-<name>`, as `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` does for
  both plural forms.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Recipes

**Add a string.** Add the key to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` in the right group, use it via
`ctx.Locale.Tr` or `trN`, and leave the other locale files alone.

**Add a plural.** Two keys named `<key>_1` and `<key>_n` plus `TrN` / `trN`; the count argument
selects the form.

**Add a string the frontend needs.** Prefer a `data-` attribute or `pageData` from the handler.
Only genuinely general text belongs in the global `window.config.i18n` object.

## Gotchas

- A missing key renders as the key itself — visible in the UI but easy to miss on a rarely-hit
  branch.
- Changing an existing key's *text* is fine; changing the *key name* invalidates every existing
  translation for it.
- Only a `bindata` build embeds `options/locale` (`modules/options/options_bindata.go`) and needs a
  rebuild for a locale change. A plain build reads the files from disk at startup
  (`modules/options/options_dynamic.go`), and outside `RUN_MODE = prod` reloads them on change
  (`modules/translation/translation.go` → `WatchLocalChanges`).
- Some keys are built from an enum's name while rendering: `actions.status.%s`
  (`templates/repo/actions/runs_list.tmpl`), and five families under `repo.issues.` for a close
  reason: `close_reason.%s` and `close_as.%s` (`repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`, `filter_actions.tmpl`),
  `close_as_with_comment.%s` (`view_content.tmpl`), `closed_as.%s` (`view_content/comments.tmpl`)
  and `closed_title_as.%s` (`shared/close_reason_icon.tmpl`). Grepping the full key finds no use, so
  grep the prefix before deleting a key that looks unused, and give a new enum value a key in every
  family that builds from it.

## Related

- `templates.md` — `ctx.Locale.Tr` and where strings are used
- `frontend-js.md` — the TypeScript side

# jj in the course repo

This repo is colocated: `.jj/` sits beside `.git/`. jj is the tool you drive, and git, GitHub and `gh` still see normal branches and commits. jj's bookmarks are git's branches.

Course rules from `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md` and `AGENTS.md` still apply word for word. jj changes the commands, not the rules:

- One issue per branch, named `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-…` or `chore/…`.
- Commit messages are Conventional Commits ending in `(#N)`, plus an `Assisted-by: Claude Code:<model id>` trailer. Never add `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by`.
- **A human approves every commit before it's made.** Approval doesn't carry over to later commits.
- Pick up new `main` work by merging it into your branch, never by rebasing. Never rebase or squash once review has started, and never force-push.
- Never merge another feature branch into yours. PRs target `main`.

## Before any jj command: are you in a git worktree?

Claude Code's isolated agents and `EnterWorktree` work in plain git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. Those have no `.jj/` of their own, so jj climbs up and answers for the main checkout instead. Tested on jj 0.46: in a worktree with a modified and a new file, `jj st` said "The working copy has no changes", and `jj describe` rewrote the main checkout's change.

So check first:

```bash
[ "$(jj root 2>/dev/null)" = "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" ] || echo "in a git worktree: don't use jj"
```

If they differ, you're in a git worktree. Run no jj commands there, and use plain git with the course rules applied by hand, because jj's immutability guard doesn't reach this checkout:

1. Tell the user you're in a git worktree and will use plain git.
2. Check the branch name with `git branch --show-current`. A harness name such as `worktree-agent-57` breaks the course naming, so rename it first: `git branch -m feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog`.
3. Show the message and `git diff --stat` (with new files listed from `git status --short`), then wait for approval. Commit only the files that belong to the change: `git add <paths>`, then `git commit -m "<message>"` with the `Assisted-by` trailer after a blank line.
4. Push with `git push -u origin <branch>`. Never pass `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, and never amend or rebase anything already pushed. A fix goes in a new commit.

## Never open an editor

A jj command that opens `$EDITOR` or a merge tool waits for input an agent never sends, and hangs. Always pass the message or the paths:

- `jj describe -m`, `jj commit -m`, and `jj new -m` when you want a message.
- `jj squash --from <rev> --into <rev> -m`, and `jj split <paths> -m`.
- Never run bare `jj describe`, `jj commit`, `jj squash -i`, `jj split`, `jj diffedit` or `jj resolve`.

## The repo's jj config (already set)

`jj config list --repo` should show:

```
revset-aliases."trunk()" = "main@origin"
revset-aliases."immutable_heads()" = "builtin_immutable_heads() | remote_bookmarks()"
user.name = "Ethan Turner"
snapshot.auto-track = "~root:ai-logs"
```

- **`immutable_heads()`** makes every pushed commit immutable, so `jj describe`, `jj squash`, `jj rebase` and `jj abandon` on pushed work fail with "Commit … is immutable". This is the guard that keeps the no-rewrite rule. Without it, `jj git push` silently force-pushes a rewritten commit, reporting it as "move sideways". Never pass `--ignore-immutable`. If a command hits the guard, the right move is a new commit on top.
- **`snapshot.auto-track`** keeps new files under `ai-logs/` out of whatever change you're on, because jj otherwise records every new file automatically. Add logs on purpose with `jj file track <paths>`.
- The email comes from the user's global jj config (the GitHub noreply address). Never commit with the wm.edu address.

If any of these are missing, restore them with `jj config set --repo …`. To quote a fileset, write `'"~root:ai-logs"'`.

## What a "commit" is in jj

The working copy is always a commit (`@`), and jj saves your edits into it automatically. A course "commit" means sealing `@` with a message: `jj commit -m "<message>"`. That gives `@` its description and starts a fresh empty `@` on top.

Before running `jj commit`, show the user the message and `jj diff --stat` (or the full `jj diff`), then wait for approval. Write the message with the trailer after a blank line:

```bash
jj commit -m "feat(shortcut): open a help dialog with ? (#57)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5"
```

The commit is now `@-`. Move the branch to it with `jj bookmark set <branch> -r @-`. Bookmarks don't follow new commits on their own, and an unmoved bookmark pushes stale code.

## Workflows

**Start an issue.** This replaces `git switch main; git pull; git switch -c`:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new main@origin                                # empty change on fresh main
# ...edit, then commit with approval as above...
jj bookmark create feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog -r @-
```

**Push and open the PR.** Push one named bookmark at a time, never `--all`:

```bash
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
gh pr create --head feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog --base main --title "…" --body-file <file>
```

Read the push output. `add to` and `move forward` are fine. `move sideways` or `move backward` means history was rewritten: stop and tell the user before anything else happens.

`gh pr create` always needs `--head`. git has no current branch in a jj repo (`git status` says `HEAD (no branch)`), so `gh` can't infer it. The PR body uses the course format from `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, including `## Tech Debt` and `Closes #N`.

**Review follow-ups.** Add new commits on top. Never amend or squash:

```bash
jj new feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
# ...edit, then commit with approval...
jj bookmark set feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog -r @-
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
```

**Sync with main.** Merge, don't rebase. The merge is itself a commit, so the user approves it too:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog main@origin -m "Merge branch 'main' into feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5"
jj new                                            # seal the merge
jj bookmark set feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog -r @-
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
```

Like every commit, the merge carries the `Assisted-by` trailer.

If the merge has conflicts, `jj st` lists them. Resolve them by editing the conflict markers in the files (not with `jj resolve`, which opens a merge tool), run `jj st` to confirm none remain, then push.

**Rewording or tidying work you haven't pushed.** `jj describe`, `jj squash` and `jj split` are allowed on commits that were never pushed, because review hasn't started on them. The immutability guard tells you where that line is.

**Issues that depend on each other** (#60 needs #57). Never base a PR on another feature branch and never merge #57's branch into #60's. You may build #60 locally on top of #57 without pushing it or giving it a bookmark. Once #57 merges into `main`, move the unpushed #60 work onto `main` (a rebase is allowed here because nothing was pushed), then bookmark and push it:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj rebase -s <first #60 change> -d main@origin
jj bookmark create feat/issue-60-… -r <last #60 change>
```

**Review a teammate's PR.** Look at it without making a git branch:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new feat/issue-59-c-shortcuts@origin          # their branch, read-only to you
# build, run /verify, read the code
jj new main@origin                                # leave; jj drops the empty change
```

**Commit AI logs.** Files under `ai-logs/` aren't tracked until you say so. Follow `/file-ai-logs` for naming and the issue comment. Then, on the branch the log belongs to:

```bash
jj new <branch>                                   # or main@origin for a chore/ai-log-… branch
jj file track ai-logs/sprint2/controlled-opposition/<log files>
jj commit -m "chore(ai-log): add <slug> (#N)"     # with approval
jj bookmark set <branch> -r @-
```

**After the PR merges.** This replaces `git switch main; git pull; git branch -d; git push --delete`:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new main@origin
jj bookmark delete feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog        # pushes the deletion to GitHub
```

Deleting the remote branch is outward-facing, so run that push as its own command after the user's OK. If a permission check blocks it, stop and hand the command to the user; don't try another route.

## Traps found in testing

- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch` closes PRs that target the deleted branch.** It doesn't retarget them, and this repo has GitHub's automatic head-branch deletion off. Course PRs target `main`, so this only matters if someone breaks that rule.
- **Tools that read git:**
  - Claude Code's git status and `git status` will show `HEAD (no branch)`. That's normal.
  - `/verify`'s doctor still checks build freshness against `HEAD`.
  - In the main checkout, don't run `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git rebase` or `git merge` (a git worktree is the one exception, above): jj imports their effects, but they bypass the immutability guard and the approval flow. Read-only git commands (`git log`, `git diff`, `git show`) are fine.
- **jj 0.46 CLI differences:** global flags like `--quiet` go before the subcommand, and `jj git push --allow-new` no longer exists (new bookmarks push without it).

## Undo

`jj undo` reverses the last jj operation, and `jj op log` lists every operation so `jj op restore <id>` can roll back further. Both work only locally. Undoing after a push leaves GitHub unchanged, and the next push would then be a force-push. So if a pushed state is wrong, fix it with a new commit, never by undoing and pushing again.

import {env} from 'node:process';

import {apiCreateBranch, apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, assertNoJsError, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

async function createRepo(page: Page) {
  const repoName = `e2e-shortcut-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, repoName, 'other.txt', 'other file');
  return `/${env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER}/${repoName}`;
}

// presses a shortcut that leaves the page, and waits until the next page can take one
async function goWith(page: Page, keys: string, url: RegExp) {
  for (const key of keys.split(' ')) await page.keyboard.press(key);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(url);
  await page.waitForLoadState();
}

  await expect(searchHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');

  await expect(search).toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.type('st');

  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('');

  await page.keyboard.press('t');

  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g c"]')).toHaveAttribute('href', `${repoLink}/src/branch/feature`);

  await goWith(page, 'g c', new RegExp(`${repoLink}$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g i', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/issues$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g p', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/pulls$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g a', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/actions$`));
  await goWith(page, 'g w', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/wiki$`));
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g shortcuts are missing for tabs that are not shown or that leave Gitea', async ({page}) => {
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
  await apiEditRepo(page.request, owner, repoName, {
    has_pull_requests: false,
    has_actions: false,
    has_issues: true,
    external_tracker: {external_tracker_url: 'https://tracker.example.com/'},
    has_wiki: true,
    external_wiki: {external_wiki_url: 'https://wiki.example.com/'},
  });
  await page.goto(repoLink);
  await expect(page.locator('.overflow-menu-items a[href="https://tracker.example.com/"]')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.locator('.overflow-menu-items a[href="https://wiki.example.com/"]')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys^="g "]')).toHaveCount(1); // only g c

  for (const keys of ['g i', 'g p', 'g a', 'g w']) {
    for (const key of keys.split(' ')) await page.keyboard.press(key);
  }
  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // a live shortcut still runs after them
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]')).toBeFocused();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g shortcuts work for tabs moved into the "more" menu', async ({page}) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({width: 420, height: 800});
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  await page.goto(repoLink);
  await expect(page.locator('.overflow-menu-popup [data-shortcut-keys="g w"]')).toBeAttached(); // the Wiki tab no longer fits
  await goWith(page, 'g w', new RegExp(`${repoLink}/wiki$`));
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('g n goes to notifications when signed in, outside any repository', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto('/explore/repos');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g n"]')).toHaveCount(0); // signed out
  await login(page);
  await page.goto('/explore/repos');
  const bell = page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys="g n"]');
  await expect(bell).toHaveCount(1); // the bell is in the page twice, only one copy declares it
  await expect(bell).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-description', 'Notifications');
  await expect(bell).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'General');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys^="g "]')).toHaveCount(1); // no repository shortcuts outside a repository
  await goWith(page, 'g n', /\/notifications$/);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

export function htmlEscape(s: string, ...args: Array<any>): string {
  if (args.length !== 0) throw new Error('use html or htmlRaw instead of htmlEscape'); // check legacy usages
  return s.replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/"/g, '&quot;')
    .replace(/'/g, '&#39;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
}

class rawObject {
  private readonly value: string;
  constructor(v: string) { this.value = v }
  toString(): string { return this.value }
}

export function html(tmpl: TemplateStringsArray, ...parts: Array<any>): string {
  let output = tmpl[0];
  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
    const value = parts[i];
    const valueEscaped = (value instanceof rawObject) ? value.toString() : htmlEscape(String(value));
    output = output + valueEscaped + tmpl[i + 1];
  }
  return output;
}

export function htmlRaw(s: string | TemplateStringsArray, ...tmplParts: Array<any>): rawObject {
  if (typeof s === 'string') {
    if (tmplParts.length !== 0) throw new Error("either htmlRaw('str') or htmlRaw`tmpl`");
    return new rawObject(s);
  }
  return new rawObject(html(s, ...tmplParts));
}

"""// Groups shortcuts by section in the order each section first appears, the default section first.
// A shortcut without a section belongs to the default one.
export function groupShortcuts(shortcuts: ShortcutInfo[], defaultSection: string): Map<string, ShortcutInfo[]> {
  const groups = new Map<string, ShortcutInfo[]>([[defaultSection, []]]);
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    const section = shortcut.section ?? defaultSection;
    if (!groups.has(section)) groups.set(section, []);
    groups.get(section)!.push(shortcut);
  }
  return groups;
}

function renderShortcutKeys(keys: string): string {
  return keys.split(' ').map((key) => html`<kbd>${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`).join('');
}

// the help dialog lists the shortcuts registered when it opens, so it also shows ones added after page load
export function initShortcutHelp(dialog: HTMLDialogElement) {
  const general = dialog.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section')!;
  registerShortcut({
    keys: dialog.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: dialog.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: general,
    element: dialog,
    action: () => {
      const groups = groupShortcuts(getShortcuts(), general);
      dialog.querySelector('.shortcut-help-sections')!.innerHTML = Array.from(groups, ([section, shortcuts]) => html`
        <section>
          <h3>${section}</h3>
          <dl>${htmlRaw(shortcuts.map((s) => html`<div class="shortcut-help-row"><dt>${s.description}</dt><dd>${htmlRaw(renderShortcutKeys(s.keys))}</dd></div>`).join(''))}</dl>
        </section>
      `).join('');
      const opener = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      dialog.addEventListener('close', () => opener.focus(), {once: true}); // browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes
      dialog.showModal();
    },
  });
}

// the markup of templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl and RepoFileSearch.vue
function renderHint(key: string, placeholder: string, section?: string) {
  const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
  wrapper.className = 'ui input global-shortcut-wrapper';
  wrapper.innerHTML = `<input placeholder="${placeholder}"><kbd data-shortcut-keys="${key}">${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`;
  document.body.append(wrapper);
  const input = wrapper.querySelector('input')!;
  const kbd = wrapper.querySelector('kbd')!;
  if (section) kbd.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  initShortcutKbd(kbd);
  return {wrapper, input, kbd};
}

// a tab link, whose text also holds an open count
function renderLink(keys: string, href: string, description: string, section?: string, shortcutHref?: string) {
  const link = document.createElement('a');
  link.href = href;
  link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-keys', keys);
  link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-description', description);
  if (section) link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  if (shortcutHref) link.setAttribute('data-shortcut-href', shortcutHref);
  link.innerHTML = `${description} <span class="ui small label">3</span>`;
  document.body.append(link);
  initShortcutLink(link);
  return link;
}

// these tests share document.body and its focus, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('shortcut hints and links', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    initGlobalShortcut();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    document.body.replaceChildren();
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  test('AC1 pressing a hint key focuses its box and hides the hint', () => {
    const search = renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    const findFile = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    expect(press(document.body, 's').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(search.input);
    expect(search.kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);

    search.input.blur();
    press(document.body, 't');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(findFile.input);
    expect(findFile.kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('AC2 Escape in a box with a hint clears it and moves focus away', () => {
    const {input, kbd} = renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    input.focus();
    input.value = 'needle';
    press(input, 'Escape');
    expect(input.value).toBe('');
    expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(input);
    expect(kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC8 a hint that loads again keeps its key working', () => {
    const before = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    before.wrapper.remove(); // as moving through the file tree replaces the page content
    const after = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    press(document.body, 't');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(after.input);
  });

  test('AC8 a second hint for the same key on the page throws', () => {
    renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    expect(() => renderHint('s', 'Search issues…')).toThrow('conflicts with "s"');
  });

  test('AC9 a hint is listed with its box\'s placeholder and its section', () => {
    renderHint('s', 'Search code…', 'Repository');
    renderHint('t', 'Go to file', 'Repository');
    renderHint('x', 'No section');
    expect(getShortcuts()).toEqual([
      {keys: 's', description: 'Search code…', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 't', description: 'Go to file', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 'x', description: 'No section', section: undefined},
    ]);
  });

  test('#58 AC1 a link\'s shortcut goes where the link leads', () => {
    const assign = vi.spyOn(window.location, 'assign').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    renderLink('g i', 'https://gitea.example/owner/repo/issues', 'Issues');
    press(document.body, 'g');
    press(document.body, 'i');
    expect(assign).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('https://gitea.example/owner/repo/issues');
  });

  test('#58 AC2 a link\'s shortcut can go to an address of its own instead', () => {
    const assign = vi.spyOn(window.location, 'assign').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    renderLink('g c', 'https://gitea.example/owner/repo/src/branch/feature', 'Code', 'Repository', 'https://gitea.example/owner/repo');
    press(document.body, 'g');
    press(document.body, 'c');
    expect(assign).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('https://gitea.example/owner/repo');
  });

  test('#58 AC5 a link moved to another part of the page keeps its shortcut', () => {
    const assign = vi.spyOn(window.location, 'assign').mockImplementation(() => undefined);
    const link = renderLink('g p', 'https://gitea.example/owner/repo/pulls', 'Pull requests');
    const menu = document.createElement('div'); // as a narrow tab bar moves tabs into its "more" menu
    menu.style.display = 'none'; // closed
    document.body.append(menu);

    press(document.body, 'g');
    press(document.body, 'p');
    expect(assign).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('https://gitea.example/owner/repo/pulls');
  });

  test('#58 AC8 a link is listed with its own description, not its text, and its section', () => {

  });
});

# Verify the Gitea fork

The surface is the web UI served by `./gitea web`; the `/api/v1` REST API is the second surface and the way to seed state. The CLI (`./gitea admin ...`) is only used for setup.

Every run gets its own instance under `.claude/verify-runs/<run-id>/` (gitignored, because all of `.claude/` is). **Never drive `http://localhost:3000`**: that is the user's own instance (`custom/conf/app.ini`, `data/`), and the user's account `mingler` must never be touched. Several runs can live side by side; each has its own port, DB, and admin.

Helpers are in `.claude/skills/verify/bin/` (run from the repo root):

| Helper | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/gitea-verify up` | Writes a dev-mode `app.ini`, starts `./gitea web` on a free port, waits for it to answer, creates admin `verify-admin` with a random password. Prints `RUN_ID`, `URL`, `ARTIFACTS`, and an `export GITEA_VERIFY_RUN=...` line. With `--owner <pid>`, a watchdog stops the server once that process exits, even on SIGKILL; `verify-run` passes its own PID. |
| `bin/gitea-verify doctor [run]` | Read-only health check (see Doctor). Exits non-zero on FAIL. |
| `bin/gitea-verify down [run]` | Kills *our* PID only, deletes `work/` and `state.env`, moves `server.log` into the artifacts. Leaves the artifacts. |
| `bin/gitea-verify prune` | Runs `down` on every run whose server already died (`up` does this first), so killed runners leave no `work/` behind. |
| `bin/gitea-verify list` | Every run, whether it is up, and where its artifacts are. |
| `bin/drive.mjs` | Node module. `session()` opens a signed-in Playwright page on the run, plus `api()`, `capture()`, `note()`, `done()`. Also exports Playwright's auto-waiting `expect` and a standalone admin `api()`. |
| `bin/verify-run <feature\|path.mjs>... \| --all` | Runs saved recipes from `recipes/`. Reuses `$GITEA_VERIFY_RUN` when doctor passes; otherwise starts a fresh run and tears it down on exit. Doctors before driving and after any failure, prints PASS/FAIL per recipe, exits non-zero if any failed. |

`[run]` defaults to `$GITEA_VERIFY_RUN`.

## Saved recipes and mise tasks

`recipes/<feature>.mjs` is the executable proof for `features/<feature>.md`: it seeds its own uniquely named state, drives every entry point the feature file lists, and throws on the first mismatch. Run one before writing a new recipe; extend it when your change adds behaviour, and fix it in the same change as its feature file.

A local, gitignored `mise.toml` at the repo root wraps the helpers (`mise tasks ls`). It declares no `[tools]` and sets `task.run_auto_install = false`, because tools come from the flake:

| Task | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `mise run verify:build` | `direnv exec . make backend` and `make frontend` (make skips what is fresh) |
| `mise run verify:up` / `verify:doctor [run]` / `verify:down [run]` / `verify:list` | the `gitea-verify` commands, after a build for `up` |
| `mise run verify:run <feature\|path.mjs>...` | build, then `verify-run`; paths resolve from your cwd |
| `mise run verify:all` | every recipe, serially, on one fresh instance (~40 s) |
| `mise run 'verify:feature:*'` | one fresh instance per recipe, in parallel (~20 s) |

Every task has a `timeout`, so a hung server or page fails the run instead of blocking it. Without mise, call `bin/verify-run` directly. If mise refuses the config, run `mise trust` once.

## Launch

1. Build what you changed. `./gitea` embeds the commit it was built from, and doctor compares it with the tree:
   - Go changed: `make backend`
   - `templates/` or `options/` changed: nothing to build. The binary has no `bindata` tag, so it reads them from disk, and dev mode reloads templates
   - `web_src/` changed: `make frontend` (writes `public/assets`, served via `STATIC_ROOT_PATH`)
   - `pnpm` (and the pinned `go`) come from the repo's flake dev shell. The agent's Bash shell doesn't load direnv, so run `direnv exec . make frontend` (same for `make backend`)
2. `.claude/skills/verify/bin/gitea-verify up`. This takes about 5 s. It is ready when it prints `RUN_ID=`. It exits non-zero and prints the server log tail if the server dies or does not answer within 120 s.
3. `export GITEA_VERIFY_RUN=<id>` in every later command (shell state does not persist between Bash calls, so prefix it: `GITEA_VERIFY_RUN=<id> node recipe.mjs`).

The instance runs `RUN_MODE = dev`, so `/devtest/*` component pages exist (`/devtest` lists them). Captcha is off and the install is locked.

## Doctor

Run `.claude/skills/verify/bin/gitea-verify doctor <id>` first, and again whenever something looks off. It checks:

- the PID is alive and is `gitea web`
- that PID owns the port (not some other server)
- `/api/v1/version` answers
- `/devtest` is served (dev mode)
- `verify-admin` authenticates
- `./gitea` freshness: WARN when Go files (or `go.mod`/`go.sum`) changed since the commit it was built from
- frontend freshness: WARN when anything in `web_src/` is newer than `public/assets/.vite/manifest.json`

A WARN means the instance runs old code. Rebuild and restart before proving anything about your change. A proof made against a stale binary proves nothing.

## Drive

Write a recipe `.mjs` in the scratchpad and run it with `GITEA_VERIFY_RUN=<id> node <recipe>.mjs`. Import the helper by absolute path. A scratchpad script cannot resolve repo packages, and `drive.mjs` resolves `@playwright/test` from the repo for you:

```js
import {session} from '/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/.claude/skills/verify/bin/drive.mjs';
const s = await session({name: 'issue-comment'}); // browser: 'webkit' too; login: false for anonymous; user/password for another account
const {page, api, user} = s;                       // user === 'verify-admin'
try {
  await api('POST', '/user/repos', {name: 'verify-issues', auto_init: true}); // seed via REST, not the UI
  await api('POST', `/repos/${user}/verify-issues/issues`, {title: 'Verify comment flow'});
  await page.goto(`/${user}/verify-issues/issues/1`, {waitUntil: 'load'});
  await s.capture('before');                       // NN-before.png + NN-before.aria.yml
  // ...the user action, through the UI...
  await s.capture('after');
  s.note('api-state', await api('GET', `/repos/${user}/verify-issues/issues/1`)); // side effect, second view
  s.done();                                        // throws if the page threw: call it last inside try
} finally { await s.close(); }                     // writes js-errors.json
```

`expect` (exported by `drive.mjs`) gives Playwright's auto-waiting assertions outside the test runner: prefer `await expect(locator).toHaveText(...)` to reading a value once and comparing it.

Rules that each cost a failed run before:

- **`waitUntil: 'load'`, never `'networkidle'`.** Signed-in pages hold an SSE connection open, so `networkidle` never fires.
- **Browsers:** chromium and webkit work. Firefox 1532 hangs at launch on this Mac (a sandbox_extension error). Do not use it; Firefox is checked only in CI.
- **WebKit skips buttons on Tab** (like Safari). Keyboard-Tab proofs run in chromium.
- **Locators:** use the same handles the e2e suite uses: `getByRole(..., {name})`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`. `tests/e2e/*.test.ts` has a working selector for most pages, so read the matching test before inventing one.
- **Fomantic dropdowns** (`.ui.dropdown`) are not ARIA menus. Click the `.ui.dropdown` and then `.menu .item` with `hasText`. Scope to the enclosing form or group, because pages often have several dropdowns.
- **Another user:** create them with `api('POST', '/admin/users', {..., must_change_password: false})`, then `session({name, user, password})` signs the browser in as them. `api()` stays admin; add `?sudo=<user>` to call the API as them. The browser cookie doesn't authenticate `/api/v1`.
- **Seed with `api()`, act with `page`.** The proof must go through the UI path the user takes; the API is for setup and for reading back the stored result.
- If the Bash sandbox blocks the browser launch, rerun that one command with the sandbox disabled.

The feature map is [`features/README.md`](features/README.md), with a saved recipe per feature in `recipes/`. Read the matching feature file, and run its recipe, before you drive.

## Evidence

Artifacts go to `.claude/verify-runs/<id>/artifacts/<session name>/`, numbered in capture order:

- `NN-<what>.png`: full-page screenshot. The footer shows the build version, `1.27.3+csci435-...-g<sha>`, which identifies the build.
- `NN-<what>.aria.yml`: an ARIA snapshot of the same moment. Assert names and states against this, not against pixels.
- `NN-<what>.json`: from `s.note()`, the stored state read back through the API.
- `js-errors.json`: uncaught page errors. Anything other than `[]` fails the proof.
- `../server.log`: moved here by `down`.

Proof standards:

- Exercise the real user path: clicks, keys, form submits. Do not call internal JS, use test-only endpoints, or set state directly.
- Capture both the action and the resulting state, not only the final screen: before, after, and the API read-back of the side effect (row stored, issue state changed, comment exists).
- When a feature has several entry points, the map lists them. Driving one entry point does not verify the others, so report which one you drove.
- For PR screenshots, Read the PNG to check it shows what you claim, then follow the screenshot conventions in memory (`commit-and-pr-conventions`).

## Cleanup

`.claude/skills/verify/bin/gitea-verify down <id>`. It kills only the PID recorded at launch: never `pkill gitea`, which would also kill the user's :3000 instance. It removes the DB and repos and keeps `artifacts/`. Run it after failed attempts too. `gitea-verify list` shows stragglers. Delete old artifact dirs only when the user asks.

## Isolation notes

- Each run's data lives under `work/`, and it never reads `custom/conf/app.ini` or `data/`.
- `verify-admin`'s password is random per run and stored in `state.env` (mode 600). It is throwaway, but still don't print it. `drive.mjs` reads it for you.
- The user's `claude-dev` account and `$GITEA_DEV_*` belong to the :3000 instance. This skill never needs them.

#57 is implemented and tested, but not committed yet; it needs your OK first. All 9 acceptance criteria are covered.

**How it works**
- **Dialog:** a native `<dialog>` in `templates/base/footer.tmpl`. The server renders the title, the close button's label and the "General" heading from three new locale keys (`shortcuts.help.title`, `.show`, `.close`). The close button is a plain form button, so closing needs no JavaScript.
- **Opening it:** `?` registers through #56's `registerShortcut`. Each time the dialog opens, it rebuilds its rows from `getShortcuts()`. A new exported `groupShortcuts()` groups them by section, with General first; a shortcut without a section goes under General. Closing returns focus to whatever had it before.
- **AC8:** I added one guard to the registry: while any `dialog[open]` exists, no shortcut runs, `?` included. That also covers AC7. #60 and later dialogs get this for free.

**Tests**
- **Unit:** all 27 pass. The new ones cover grouping (AC5), the dialog's rows and HTML escaping, focus returning on close, and shortcuts being blocked while it's open. I removed the guard once to confirm the AC8 test fails without it.
- **E2E:** the new test passes in Chromium and WebKit, and all 16 Chromium and WebKit runs pass. All 8 Firefox runs failed only because Firefox won't launch on this Mac; it runs only in CI.
- **Lint:** lint-js, lint-css and lint-templates are clean, with no trailing whitespace. `make lint-json` fails on `data/indexers/issues.bleve/index_meta.json`, a local file outside the repo's changes.
- **`/verify`:** I drove a real instance with no JS errors and checked screenshots in the dark theme and at 375px, after one CSS fix for heading spacing. The 375px shot is also dark, and there's no final light-theme shot because the first run saved the dark theme, so I'll retake light at PR time. Six Tabs kept focus inside the dialog, and Escape put focus back where it was.

# Issue #56 -- Central keyboard-shortcut registry with chords

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](56-ab-wm-class.png)

**Notation.** This issue is TypeScript, Vue and Go templates rather than Go, so the diagram maps
them as follows. A TypeScript `class` is a UML class. A module (a file of functions and
module-level variables, such as `shortcut.ts`) is a class with the «module» stereotype: exported
functions are `+`, unexported ones `-`. A TypeScript `type` is a class with «type», a Vue component
is a «component» with its props as attributes, a Go template is a «template» with the attributes it
renders, and a browser custom element is a «custom element». A `data-global-init` attribute that
makes one file run another's code is drawn as a dependency. In Go code the same approach maps a
struct to a class, an interface to an «interface» that structs realize, and struct embedding to
composition.

## Sequence Diagram

```text
# Pele

Pele renders [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org) diagrams to SVG. It is small, synchronous, has no runtime dependencies, and uses CSS variables for colors and fonts.

Pele supports every diagram type built into Mermaid 12.1.0.

Documentation, examples, and a playground are at [pele.run](https://pele.run).

## Install

```sh
npm install pele
```

Or load it [from a CDN](https://pele.run/api#using-a-cdn):

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pele@1/dist/pele.global.js"></script>
<script>
  for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('pre.mermaid')) pele.mount(el, el.textContent);
</script>
```

## Use

```ts
import { render } from 'pele';

const { svg } = render(`flowchart LR
  A[Mermaid text] --> B[SVG]`);

document.querySelector('#diagram').innerHTML = svg;
```

In a browser, `mount()` renders into an element, reads fonts from CSS, and adapts the layout to the container width:

```ts
import { mount } from 'pele';

mount(document.querySelector('#diagram'), text);
```

See the [API](https://pele.run/api) for options and error handling.

The main entry point includes every diagram type. Reduce the initial bundle size by registering individual types or loading them on demand:

```ts
import { register, render } from 'pele/core';
import flowchart from 'pele/diagrams/flowchart';

register(flowchart);
```

```ts
import { renderAsync } from 'pele/lazy';

const { svg } = await renderAsync(text);
```

## Theme

Set CSS variables on the diagram or a parent element to customize colors and fonts:

```css
.pele {
  --pele-bg: #fffcf0;
  --pele-fg: #100f0f;
  --pele-muted: #6f6e69;
  --pele-line: #100f0f;
  --pele-surface: #f2f0e5;
  --pele-surface-alt: #e6e4d9;
  --pele-border: #cecdc3;
  --pele-accent: #205ea6;
  --pele-font: sans-serif;
  --pele-radius: 4px;
}
```

Charts use `--pele-series-1` through `--pele-series-8`. Colors adapt to theme changes without being re-rendered. See [Theming](https://pele.run/theming) for all variables, fonts, and class names.

## Security

Pele escapes diagram text, filters links and styles, and limits source and output size. See [Security](https://pele.run/security) for handling untrusted diagrams, displaying errors, and supplying icons.

## Compatibility

Pele targets Mermaid 12.1.0 syntax, with its own layout and visual style. Its parsers are tested against Mermaid's parser specs and with differential fuzzing.

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm test
npm run build
npm run bench
```

`npm run bench:mermaid` times Pele and Mermaid.js in headless Chrome on the same diagrams and compares bundle sizes. It needs Node 22 or later. It fetches Mermaid 12.1.0 from unpkg; pass `-- --mermaid <version>` for another release, and set `CHROME` if Chrome is not in `/Applications`.

The documentation site and playground are in `website/` and use Node 24 and pnpm 12. With nvm:

```sh
cd website
nvm use
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

After installing the website dependencies, run `npm run test:website` from the repository root to check the playground.

See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for parser testing.

## License

MIT. The specs under `tests/compat` and the grammar files beside them come from Mermaid, which is also MIT licensed.
```
</details></tool-use>
